summary: Three good IELTS-style passages (849-891 words) on weather forecasting, urban wetlands and habits, getting harder from 1 to 3, with a full range of question types and mostly well-paraphrased questions. Two groups were out of passage order (a summary in Passage 2 and the Yes/No/Not Given set in Passage 3); both are now reordered. All answer keys were correct.
strengths: Passage 1 completion items paraphrase rather than copy (felt/sense, vast/enormous, transmitting photographs/sent back pictures), and TFNG traps are well judged (Q9 'fishing' appears in the text but says nothing about funding).

Passage 2 has seven lettered paragraphs, a five-name people match with one unused name, and information-matching items that require paraphrase (organisms/bacteria; destroyed/drained, filled and buried).
Passage 3 is an argued text at C1 level; sentence endings include distractors that reverse the passage (C, F).
Key quality is high: every FALSE/NO is directly contradicted and every NOT GIVEN is genuinely absent.
